support.intro: Support from corporations and individual donors provides critical resources to supplement operational and external research funding for the Center. These funds allow CalPlug to expand outreach and education and to conduct independent research on the future of plug loads, energy efficiency and storage, and user experience.

ways.name: Friend of CalPlug
ways.how: Send a gift by check payable to "The UCI Foundation", mailed to: California Plug Load Research Center (CalPlug), ATTN: Herumi Baylon, University of California, Irvine, Irvine, CA 92697-2800. To donate equipment or materials, contact Dr. Arnold Wang.

ways.name: Corporate Member
ways.how: To request information about becoming a member, contact Dr. Shuoyu (Arnold) Wang.
ways._flag: Membership benefits are an image (screenshot) on the current site; text must be retyped from it.

requirements: GPA 3.0+ preferred (lower GPAs considered with explanation)
Commit at least 3 quarters (1 year) of research
Work a minimum of 8 hours/week (2 units is about 8 hours)
Attend team meetings, keep a research log, and submit a short report at the end of each quarter
benefits: Dedicated workspace, supplies, and equipment provided
Mentorship from faculty and project leaders
Opportunity to earn 1-3 course credits (199/299) and possibly paid positions after 2+ quarters of outstanding work
Letters of recommendation for committed students (after 2+ quarters)

facilities.name: SIM Lab
facilities.summary: The CalPlug Engineering Lab collects energy consumption and performance data for plug load devices. CalPlug works with manufacturers and utilities to test prototypes before production or pilot programs, using industry testing standards such as ENERGY STAR, IEC and CEA. Four demonstration labs are set up as SIM labs, such as the SIM living room and the SIM office.

facilities.name: SIM Home
facilities.summary: The Simulation, Integration, and Management (SIM) Home is an advanced metering and observation environment for studying user behavior patterns while monitoring energy consumption, with networked plug load device testing.

facilities.name: 1 kWh Challenge
facilities.summary: A community outreach and education program in which UCI community members learned exactly how much energy a kilowatt-hour is.
